title: DHM Price Per mg Compared: Which Supplement Is the Best Value?
excerpt: We did the math on 8 DHM supplements. Plain DHM costs about 5 to 13 cents per 100mg; branded hangover formulas cost 2 to 25 times more. Here's the full table and how to check any product yourself.
metaDescription: DHM price per mg for 8 supplements, from about 5 cents to $1.21 per 100mg. See the full table, cost per dose and per year, and how to do the math yourself.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The answer first:** at the prices we last recorded, plain single-ingredient DHM is far cheaper per milligram than branded hangover formulas. **NusaPure DHM 1,000mg** came out cheapest at about **5 cents per 100mg**, followed by **Double Wood** at about **8 cents** and **DHM Depot** at about **13 cents**. Premium blends like Cheers Restore, Fuller Health After Party and No Days Wasted cost roughly 2 to 6 times more per milligram of DHM, and Flyby Recovery costs about 25 times more. The gap mostly pays for extra ingredients and packaging, not more DHM.

This page shows the full math, explains how to check any product yourself in under a minute, and covers when paying more might still make sense for you.

> **Prices change.** Every figure here comes from the list prices and pack sizes we last recorded for each product. Amazon prices move with sales, subscriptions and pack-size changes, so treat this as a method and a rough ranking, then recheck the live listing before you buy. Nothing here is medical advice. If you take prescription medicines, are pregnant, or have liver or kidney problems, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any supplement, including DHM.

## DHM Price Per mg: The Full Comparison Table

Here is every DHM product we track, ranked from cheapest to most expensive per 100mg of DHM. "Total DHM" is the DHM per serving multiplied by the number of servings in the pack.

| Product | Price | Servings | DHM per serving | Total DHM | Cost per 100mg DHM | Cost per serving |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NusaPure DHM 1,000mg | $28.99 | 60 | 1,000mg | 60,000mg | **$0.048** | $0.48 |
| Double Wood DHM | $23.95 | 30 | 1,000mg | 30,000mg | **$0.080** | $0.80 |
| DHM Depot | $19.95 | 50 | 300mg | 15,000mg | **$0.133** | $0.40 |
| No Days Wasted DHM Detox | $28.99 | 15 | 1,000mg | 15,000mg | $0.193 | $1.93 |
| Toniiq Ease | $24.97 | 40 | 300mg | 12,000mg | $0.208 | $0.62 |
| Cheers Restore | $34.99 | 12 | 1,000mg | 12,000mg | $0.292 | $2.92 |
| Fuller Health After Party | $59.99 | 30 | 650mg | 19,500mg | $0.308 | $2.00 |
| Flyby Recovery | $14.49 | 4 | 300mg | 1,200mg | $1.208 | $3.62 |

Two things jump out. First, the cheapest bottle up front (Flyby at $14.49) is by far the most expensive per milligram, because it holds only 1,200mg of DHM in total. Second, "cost per serving" and "cost per mg" tell very different stories. DHM Depot has the lowest cost per serving at 40 cents, but each serving holds only 300mg, so per milligram it sits behind NusaPure and Double Wood.

## Why Price Per mg Is the Number That Matters

Shelf price tells you what you pay today. Price per serving tells you what one dose costs, but only if every brand defines a "serving" the same way, and they don't. One brand's serving is a single 300mg capsule. Another's is two capsules totaling 1,000mg. A third bundles DHM with a dozen other ingredients and calls the whole packet a serving.

Price per milligram of DHM strips all of that away. It answers one simple question: how much are you paying for the active ingredient you're actually shopping for? Once you know that, you can decide whether the extras in a premium formula are worth the markup to you.

It's the same logic as the unit price label on a grocery shelf. A big box of cereal can cost more than a small one and still be the better deal.

## How to Calculate DHM Price Per mg Yourself

You only need three numbers from the label and the listing:

1. **The price** of the bottle or pack.
2. **The DHM per serving**, from the supplement facts panel. Use the DHM line, not the total capsule weight or a "proprietary blend" total.
3. **The number of servings** in the container.

Then:

- **Total DHM** = DHM per serving x number of servings
- **Price per mg** = price / total DHM
- **Price per 100mg** = price per mg x 100 (easier to compare, since the raw per-mg numbers are tiny)

**Worked example (Double Wood):** 1,000mg x 30 servings = 30,000mg of DHM. $23.95 / 30,000 = $0.0008 per mg, which is 8 cents per 100mg.

**Worked example (Flyby Recovery):** 300mg x 4 servings = 1,200mg of DHM. $14.49 / 1,200 = about $0.012 per mg, or roughly $1.21 per 100mg.

### Watch out for these label traps

- **Capsules vs servings.** Many products list a serving as two or three capsules. If the bottle says "60 capsules" and the serving is 2 capsules, you have 30 servings, not 60.
- **Extract weight vs DHM content.** A label might list "1,200mg vine tea extract (98% DHM)". The DHM in that is about 1,176mg. That's close enough not to matter much. But if a label lists an extract or herb weight with no DHM percentage, you can't work out the real DHM content, and you should treat the price per mg as unknown.
- **Proprietary blends.** If DHM is buried inside a blend with one combined weight, the label doesn't tell you how much DHM you're getting. That makes a fair price comparison impossible.
- **Subscribe-and-save and multipacks.** Discounts change the math. Recalculate with the price you'd actually pay.

## Cost Per Dose: Adjusting for How Much DHM You Actually Take

Price per mg is the fairest comparison, but what you really care about is what a night out costs you. That depends on your dose.

There is no firmly established human dose for DHM. Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) uses about **300mg to 600mg per drinking session** as a working range, with around **500mg** for most adults. Many products give you 1,000mg per serving, which is more than that range.

Here's what a 500mg dose would cost from each product, based on price per mg:

| Product | Cost of a 500mg dose | Cost of their standard serving |
|---|---|---|
| NusaPure | $0.24 | $0.48 (1,000mg) |
| Double Wood | $0.40 | $0.80 (1,000mg) |
| DHM Depot | $0.67 | $0.40 (300mg) |
| No Days Wasted | $0.97 | $1.93 (1,000mg) |
| Toniiq Ease | $1.04 | $0.62 (300mg) |
| Cheers Restore | $1.46 | $2.92 (1,000mg) |
| Fuller Health After Party | $1.54 | $2.00 (650mg) |
| Flyby Recovery | $6.04 | $3.62 (300mg) |

**The practical catch:** you can only take "500mg" if the capsules let you. If a 1,000mg serving is two 500mg capsules, taking one capsule halves your cost per night. If it's a single 1,000mg capsule, you can't split it neatly, and your real cost is the full serving. Check the label for capsule size before counting on this saving.

Going the other way, a 300mg product like DHM Depot or Toniiq Ease means taking two servings to reach roughly 600mg, which doubles the per-night cost shown on the listing.

## What It Costs Over a Year

Small per-dose differences add up. Say you drink socially about once a week, roughly 48 nights a year, and take one standard serving each time:

| Product | Yearly cost (one standard serving, 48 nights) |
|---|---|
| DHM Depot | about $19 |
| NusaPure | about $23 |
| Toniiq Ease | about $30 |
| Double Wood | about $38 |
| No Days Wasted | about $93 |
| Fuller Health After Party | about $96 |
| Cheers Restore | about $140 |
| Flyby Recovery | about $174 |

Note that the products with smaller servings (DHM Depot and Toniiq Ease at 300mg) look cheapest here because each serving holds less DHM. If you matched everyone to the same 500mg dose, NusaPure would cost about $12 a year and Double Wood about $19, while Flyby would run close to $290.

The takeaway: over a year of regular social drinking, the difference between a plain DHM bottle and a premium branded formula can easily be $100 or more for roughly the same amount of DHM.

## Product-by-Product Value Notes

Price per mg isn't the only thing that matters. Here's an honest look at what you get, and give up, with each option.

### NusaPure DHM 1,000mg: lowest cost per mg

- **Pros:** Cheapest DHM per milligram in our comparison. 60 servings per bottle. Single-ingredient formula, so you know exactly what you're paying for. Listed at 98%+ purity.
- **Cons:** Fewer customer reviews than the big names. No supporting ingredients, if you want those. A 1,000mg serving is above the dose many people need, so check whether the capsules can be split.

Our [NusaPure DHM review](/never-hungover/nusapure-dhm-review-analysis) goes deeper.

### Double Wood DHM: best-known budget option

- **Pros:** Second cheapest per mg. A large number of reviews and a long track record on Amazon. Plain DHM at 1,000mg per serving.
- **Cons:** Only 30 servings, so you'll rebuy more often than with NusaPure. Basic, no-frills formula.

See our [Double Wood DHM review](/never-hungover/double-wood-dhm-review-analysis) for more.

### DHM Depot: lowest cost per serving, smaller doses

- **Pros:** Lowest price per serving at 40 cents. 300mg servings make it easy to fine-tune your dose. Single ingredient.
- **Cons:** At 300mg a serving, many adults will take two, which puts the real nightly cost above Double Wood's. Third on price per mg.

### No Days Wasted DHM Detox: premium formula, mid-range per mg

- **Pros:** 1,000mg DHM plus L-cysteine, milk thistle, prickly pear, B vitamins and electrolytes in one serving. Popular and well reviewed.
- **Cons:** About 2.4 times Double Wood's price per mg and 4 times NusaPure's. Only 15 servings per pack. There's no good evidence that the added ingredients make a meaningful difference to hangovers in people.

### Toniiq Ease: DHM plus reishi and milk thistle

- **Pros:** Combines DHM with reishi mushroom and milk thistle, which some people want for general liver support. 40 servings. Reasonable cost per serving.
- **Cons:** Only 300mg of DHM per serving, and the serving is several capsules, so reaching a 500mg to 600mg dose takes a lot of pills. Mid-pack on price per mg.

### Cheers Restore: well-known brand, premium price

- **Pros:** One of the most recognized hangover brands, with thousands of reviews. Combines DHM with L-cysteine, prickly pear, B vitamins and ginger. The listing describes roughly 1,200mg of vine tea extract at 98% DHM per dose.
- **Cons:** Around 6 times NusaPure's price per mg. Only 12 doses per pack. Customer experiences are mixed. See our [Cheers Restore review](/never-hungover/cheers-restore-review).

### Fuller Health After Party: highest shelf price

- **Pros:** 650mg of DHM per serving, close to the commonly used range. 30 servings.
- **Cons:** At $59.99 it has the highest shelf price we track, and one of the highest costs per mg. You're paying for brand and formulation.

### Flyby Recovery: convenience pack, worst per-mg value

- **Pros:** Small packs are easy to try or travel with. Broad formula with amino acids, B vitamins, milk thistle, vitamin C and electrolytes. Lots of reviews.
- **Cons:** By far the most expensive DHM per milligram, about 25 times NusaPure. Only 300mg of DHM per serving. Our [Flyby Recovery review](/never-hungover/flyby-recovery-review-2025) covers the formula in detail.

## When Paying More Per mg Can Still Make Sense

Cheapest per mg is the right goal if DHM is what you want. But there are fair reasons someone might pay more:

- **You want an all-in-one product.** If you'd otherwise buy DHM, an electrolyte mix and a B-complex separately, a combined formula can be simpler. Just be honest with yourself that the extras have weak evidence for hangovers. Electrolytes can help if you're actually dehydrated, but you can get those cheaply on their own, as our [electrolyte drinks comparison](/never-hungover/electrolyte-drinks-for-hangover-compared) shows.
- **You're trying DHM for the first time.** A small pack costs more per mg but less up front. If you're not sure DHM works for you, spending $15 to find out is reasonable. If you decide you like it, switch to a bulk bottle.
- **You strongly prefer a brand you trust.** Review volume, return policies and customer service count for something. Just know what the premium is.
- **Dose flexibility.** A 300mg product lets you take 300mg, 600mg or 900mg exactly. That can be worth a small premium if you want precise control.

What doesn't justify a big premium is the idea that a pricier product contains "better" DHM. Most of the products here list similar purity (98% or so). The DHM molecule is the same.

## What Price Per mg Can't Tell You

A low unit price only matters if the label is accurate. Supplements in the US aren't approved by the FDA before they're sold, and manufacturers are responsible for what's on the label. Some things to keep in mind:

- **Look for third-party testing.** Seals from independent testing programs, or a certificate of analysis on request, give you more confidence that the DHM content is what the label says. Some listings claim third-party testing; it's worth checking the brand's site for details.
- **Check the expiration date.** A bulk bottle is only a bargain if you use it before it expires.
- **Store it properly.** Keep it cool, dry and sealed.

It's also worth being clear about what you're buying. DHM (dihydromyricetin) is a plant compound from the Japanese raisin tree and related plants. Research on alcohol metabolism and liver health is promising but comes mostly from animal and lab studies, with limited human data. There is no good evidence that DHM prevents hangovers reliably, and it doesn't reduce your blood alcohol or make it safe to drive. Our [honest look at whether DHM works](/never-hungover/does-dhm-work-honest-science-review-2025) walks through the evidence. Because the evidence is still developing, there's a strong case for not overpaying while you find out whether it helps you.

## Safety Note Before You Stock Up

Buying cheaply shouldn't mean taking more. A bigger bottle is not a reason to raise your dose. Stick to the label or the range in our dosage guide.

DHM is generally reported to be well tolerated, but long-term human safety data are limited, and it may interact with some medicines. **Talk to your doctor or pharmacist first** if you take prescription medication (especially drugs processed by the liver, blood thinners, or sedatives), are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have liver or kidney disease. Our [DHM medication interactions guide](/never-hungover/dhm-medication-interactions-safety-guide-2025) has more detail.

## The Bottom Line

If you want the most DHM for your money, a plain single-ingredient product wins by a wide margin. At the prices we last recorded, [NusaPure DHM 1,000mg](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08B32XBRB?tag=dhmguide-20) was cheapest per milligram, and [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) was a close second with a longer track record. If you prefer smaller, adjustable doses, [DHM Depot](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0767N448Q?tag=dhmguide-20) offers 300mg servings at the lowest cost per serving.

If you want an all-in-one formula and don't mind paying several times more per mg, [No Days Wasted](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) is the most reasonably priced of the premium blends we compare. For more options ranked on more than price, see our [best DHM supplements guide](/never-hungover/best-dhm-supplements), and if money is tight, our [budget DHM guide for students](/never-hungover/broke-college-student-budget-dhm-2025) has more ways to stretch a bottle.

Whatever you choose, recheck the live price, do the quick per-mg math, and remember that drinking less and slower, eating and staying hydrated do more for tomorrow morning than any supplement.

If you want to know where each brand is actually sold, including stores beyond Amazon, see our guide to [where to buy DHM](/never-hungover/where-to-buy-dhm), and our [full product reviews](/reviews) compare the formulas side by side.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the cheapest DHM supplement per mg?**

At the prices we last recorded, NusaPure DHM 1,000mg was the cheapest per milligram, at about 4.8 cents per 100mg (60 servings of 1,000mg for $28.99). Double Wood came second at about 8 cents per 100mg, and DHM Depot third at about 13 cents. Amazon prices change often, so recheck the listing and redo the math before you buy.

**How do you calculate DHM price per mg?**

Multiply the DHM per serving by the number of servings to get the total DHM in the bottle, then divide the price by that total. For example, $23.95 divided by 30,000mg (30 servings of 1,000mg) is about $0.0008 per mg, or 8 cents per 100mg. Use the DHM amount on the supplement facts panel, not the total capsule weight or the total blend weight.

**Is a more expensive DHM supplement better?**

Not necessarily. A higher price usually pays for extra ingredients (such as L-cysteine, milk thistle, B vitamins or electrolytes), branding, or smaller pack sizes, not more or better DHM. There is no good evidence that these extra ingredients make a meaningful difference to hangovers in people, so if your goal is DHM itself, a plain single-ingredient product is usually the best value.

**How much DHM do I actually need per night?**

There is no firmly established human dose. Our dosage guide uses roughly 300mg to 600mg per drinking session as a working range, with around 500mg for most adults. That matters for cost: if your product gives 1,000mg per serving and you only need about 500mg, you may be able to take half a serving and double the number of nights per bottle. Check the label first, since some capsules can't be split evenly.

**Why is Flyby so much more expensive per mg of DHM?**

Flyby Recovery packs a lot of other ingredients (amino acids, B vitamins, milk thistle, vitamin C and electrolytes) alongside 300mg of DHM, and it sells in small packs. At the price we recorded ($14.49 for 4 servings), that works out to about $1.21 per 100mg of DHM, roughly 25 times NusaPure. You're paying for the whole formula and the convenience, not for the DHM.

**Does purity affect the real price per mg?**

Yes, in principle. If a product lists 1,000mg of an extract that is 98% DHM, you're getting about 980mg of actual DHM. Most of the products we compare list 98% purity or similar, so it barely changes the ranking. It matters more if a label lists a raw herb or extract weight without saying how much of it is DHM.

**Is it worth buying in bulk to save money?**

Usually, yes, if you'll use it. Larger bottles almost always cost less per mg. The risk is buying more than you'll use before the expiration date. If you drink a few times a month, a 30 to 60 serving bottle of a plain DHM product typically lasts many months.
